categories.main_business_segments: Zscaler operates through a unified cloud security platform called the Zero Trust Exchange, which is organized into three core product segments: Zscaler for Users (providing secure internet and SaaS access via ZIA and private application access via ZPA), Zscaler for Workloads (securing cloud and data center workloads), and Zscaler for IoT/OT (providing zero trust security for connected IoT and OT devices). The company also offers complementary solutions including digital experience management (ZDX), data protection, posture control, and risk management capabilities.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Zscaler's core technology is a cloud-native, multi-tenant, globally distributed cloud platform built on a three-tier architecture comprising the Zscaler Central Authority (control plane), Zscaler Enforcement Nodes (enforcement plane), and Zscaler Log Servers (logging and statistics plane). The platform processes over 500 billion internet transactions daily across more than 160 data centers globally. Key technologies include advanced threat protection using AI/ML, cloud sandbox for zero-day exploit detection, browser isolation, data loss prevention, and cloud access security broker (CASB) capabilities. The platform is protected by more than 580 issued and pending patents.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Zscaler serves over 8,650 customers across all major geographies, with approximately 35% of the Forbes Global 2000 as customers. The customer base spans every major industry including financial services, healthcare, insurance, manufacturing, automotive, airlines and transportation, conglomerates, consumer goods and retail, media and communications, public sector and education, energy, technology, and telecommunications services. Approximately 50% of revenue comes from customers outside the United States, with no single end customer representing more than 10% of revenue.
categories.geographic_coverage: Zscaler operates globally with a distributed cloud platform spanning more than 160 data centers across five continents, serving users in over 185 countries. The company has significant international presence with approximately 63% of full-time employees located outside the United States, with the majority of non-U.S.-based employees in India. The company derives approximately 50% of revenue from international customers and maintains research and development centers in India, Canada, Israel, and Spain.
categories.supply_chain_position: Zscaler operates as a downstream provider in the cybersecurity supply chain, delivering cloud-based security solutions directly to enterprises and through channel partners. The company relies on a network of global telecommunications service providers, system integrators, value-added resellers, and public cloud marketplaces as channel partners to reach customers. The company also depends on upstream suppliers for data center equipment and components, and integrates third-party software and open source software into its platform.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Zscaler's strategic priorities include: continuing to win new customers and expand in existing customers through a land-and-expand approach; leveraging channel partners for cloud transformation initiatives; expanding and innovating services through significant R&D investment; and expanding into additional market segments including U.S. federal government and new geographies in Asia Pacific and Latin America. The company is integrating proprietary large language models and AI/ML capabilities with its Zero Trust Exchange platform to improve security outcomes. R&D expense was $499.8 million in fiscal 2024, representing significant investment in platform reliability, scalability, and new capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: Zscaler generates revenue primarily through subscription-based cloud security services. Customers subscribe to access the Zero Trust Exchange platform and its various solutions (ZIA, ZPA, ZDX, and others) on a subscription basis, typically with contract terms of one to three years. Revenue is recognized ratably over the subscription term. The company also derives revenue through channel partners who place purchase orders after receiving customer orders. Subscriptions are typically invoiced annually or multi-year in advance, contributing to deferred revenue.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Zscaler competes in the intensely competitive network security market against legacy on-premises appliance vendors, large networking vendors offering security capabilities, point solution providers (proxy, firewall, CASB, sandboxing, DLP), and other cloud-based security service providers. Major competitors include established vendors with greater financial resources, larger sales forces, broader distribution networks, and more mature intellectual property portfolios. Zscaler differentiates through its integrated cloud platform that consolidates multiple point products, though many competitors have substantially greater resources and market presence.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Zscaler is a large accelerated filer with significant scale and growth trajectory. Revenue increased from $1,090.9 million in fiscal 2022 to $1,617.0 million in fiscal 2023 to $2,167.8 million in fiscal 2024, representing year-over-year growth of 48% and 34% respectively. The company had a market capitalization of approximately $19.8 billion as of January 31, 2024. However, the company has experienced net losses of $390.3 million (fiscal 2022), $202.3 million (fiscal 2023), and $57.7 million (fiscal 2024), with an accumulated deficit of $1,148.1 million as of July 31, 2024.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Zscaler's core value proposition is delivering comprehensive cloud-native security that eliminates the need for traditional on-premises security appliances and legacy network perimeter approaches. Key differentiators include: a unified, integrated platform consolidating multiple security functions (threat protection, data protection, access control, experience management) rather than point solutions; zero trust architecture that secures users, devices, and applications regardless of location or network; processing over 500 billion daily transactions enabling rapid threat detection and blocking across the customer base (cloud security effect); and simplified operations with reduced complexity and cost compared to appliance-based solutions. The platform provides fast, secure, and reliable access while optimizing user experience.
